title: Right & oblique triangles
sentences: An oblique triangle has no 90° angle.
Label side a opposite angle A, and likewise b/B and c/C.
The sine rule connects opposite side-angle pairs.
The cosine rule finds a missing side from two sides and their included angle, or an angle from three sides.
A sine-rule problem with two sides and a non-included angle may have zero, one, or two solutions.
Two sides are 5 cm and 7 cm, with an included angle of 60°.
Two sides and their included angle are known: c² = 5² + 7² − 2(5)(7) cos 60°.
The triangle is not right, so Pythagoras alone would be wrong.
spoken: An oblique triangle has no 90 degrees angle.
Label side a opposite angle A, and likewise b divided by B and c divided by C.
The sine rule connects opposite side-angle pairs.
The cosine rule finds a missing side from two sides and their included angle, or an angle from three sides.
A sine-rule problem with two sides and a non-included angle may have zero, one, or two solutions.
Two sides are 5 centimeters and 7 centimeters, with an included angle of 60 degrees.
Two sides and their included angle are known: c squared equals 5 squared plus 7 squared minus 2(5)(7) cos 60 degrees.
c squared equals 25 plus 49 minus 70(0.5) equals 39.
c equals square root of 39 approximately 6.24 centimeters.
The triangle is not right, so Pythagoras alone would be wrong.
